title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Tax Evasion and Tax Resistance

articles.content_en: 1. Where entities or individuals with tax payment obligations (hereinafter referred to as taxpayers) violate tax laws and regulations by means of deception or concealment, pay less or no tax due, evade the performance of tax obligations, and if the circumstances are serious, the persons directly responsible shall be investigated for criminal liability for the crime of tax evasion. The means commonly used for tax evasion include: forging, altering, concealing, or destroying account books, bills, receipts, or vouchers; transferring funds, property, or accounts; failing to report or falsely reporting taxable items, quantities, income amounts, or revenue amounts; falsely increasing costs, overstating expenses, or reducing profits; fabricating facts to defraud tax reductions or exemptions, etc.

2. Where taxpayers violate tax laws and regulations, adopt open confrontation or other means to resist performing tax obligations, and if the circumstances are serious, the persons directly responsible shall be investigated for criminal liability for the crime of tax resistance. The means commonly used for tax resistance include: refusing to pay taxes or overdue fines in accordance with tax laws and regulations; delaying or resisting the payment of taxes on various pretexts; refusing to handle tax registration, tax declaration, or provide tax materials in accordance with statutory procedures; refusing to accept tax inspections lawfully conducted by tax authorities; storming, smashing, or vandalizing tax authorities, assaulting or insulting tax officials (including tax assistant collectors and deputy collectors), etc.

3. Where entities or individuals with the obligation to collect and pay taxes on behalf of the tax authority (hereinafter referred to as collection agents) or entities or individuals with the obligation to withhold and remit or collect and remit taxes (hereinafter referred to as withholding agents) commit any of the acts listed in Articles 1 and 2 above, they shall be investigated for criminal liability for the crime of tax evasion or the crime of tax resistance.

4. The term "persons directly responsible" for the crime of tax evasion or the crime of tax resistance refers to the legal representative, persons in charge, and other persons directly involved who bear direct responsibility for the crime in an entity that commits tax evasion or tax resistance, as well as individuals who commit tax evasion or tax resistance.
7. Where the amount of tax resistance reaches 50% or more of the amount standards specified in Article 5, the circumstances shall be deemed serious for tax resistance.

9. Where the same taxpayer simultaneously evades or resists two or more types of taxes, as long as one type reaches the above standard for constituting a crime, the amounts evaded or resisted for other tax types shall be included in the total amount of tax evasion or tax resistance.

10. Whoever colludes with taxpayers, collection agents, or withholding agents to provide accounts, invoices, or certificates for tax evasion crimes, or jointly commits the crime of tax evasion by other means, shall be punished as an accomplice to tax evasion.
Whoever instigates or incites taxpayers, collection agents, or withholding agents to resist tax, or jointly commits the crime of tax resistance by other means, shall be punished as an accomplice to tax resistance.
Tax officials who commit the crimes in the preceding two paragraphs shall be given severe punishment.

11. Where a person commits both the crime of tax evasion and the crime of tax resistance with respect to the same tax payment, the person shall be punished for multiple crimes.
Where injury or homicide is committed through violent tax resistance, the person shall be convicted and punished for the crime of injury or the crime of homicide, or shall be punished for multiple crimes according to the circumstances of the case.

12. Where, in handling cases of tax evasion or tax resistance, the People's Courts or People's Procuratorates discover that the registered economic nature (including the nature of ownership and the form of distribution) of a taxpayer is inconsistent with the actual situation, they shall, based on the facts found, handle the case according to law in accordance with the actual economic nature.
13. Whoever, for the purpose of profit, resells invoices, and if the circumstances are serious, shall be punished as the crime of speculation and profiteering.

14. This Interpretation shall apply to criminal cases of tax evasion and tax resistance handled after May 1, 1992.
March 16, 1992
